thread.title: Dow Jones Up After Two-Day 1,000-Point Plunge | Investor's Business Daily

author: DAVID SAITO-CHUNG
title: Dow Jones Up After Two-Day 1,000-Point Plunge | Investor's Business Daily
text:
The Dow Jones industrial average set on a new course of recovery in stocks today , rising around 0.9% in afternoon trade and taking back a small chunk of its 1,000-point pounding in the prior two days of trading.
Volume is running slightly higher on the NYSE vs. the same time Monday, another promising sign. Meanwhile, a sprinkling of leadership-quality stocks in the restaurant, retail and semiconductor sectors are trying to bottom out and help lead the next tradable market uptrend. They include Darden Restaurants ( DRI ), Chipotle Mexican Grill ( CMG ), Broadcom ( AVGO ), Big Cap 20 name Xilinx ( XLNX ) and Intel ( INTC ).
But as The Big Picture column noted Monday, now is not the time to actively hunt for top growth stocks. A future upgrade in the market outlook will boost patient growth investors' chances of making money in new buys.
The Nasdaq composite thrust a little faster into positive ground, rising 1% in afternoon trading. The Nasdaq 100-tracking Invesco QQQ Trust ETF ( QQQ ) lifted nearly 1.3%.
The Dow Jones Outperforms This Large Cap Index The S&P 500 rose less than 0.6% as the ongoing bloodletting in crude oil futures (down more than 4.8% to $47.46 a barrel) depressed virtually all stocks in the energy sector.
Naturally, industry groups that get hurt by high fuel costs — such as airlines, travel booking, paint, steel and trucks — bolstered the upside Tuesday. But an analysis of 197 IBD industry groups shows that computer, data storage, internet content and semiconductor shares also showed big gains of 2% or more.
See the entire daily performance of all 197 industry groups in the IBD Data Tables section of IBD's Stock Lists on Investors.com.
Small caps also advanced. The Russell 2000 rebounded 1%. Through Monday's close, the Russell stood 21% below its 52-week high, meeting the basic technical definition of a bear market.
Most Megacaps Are Still Struggling Volume on the Nasdaq is also running higher vs. the same time Monday. This indicates a penchant among institutional investors to actively bargain-hunt for stocks after the two-month meltdown on Wall Street.
Even beleaguered Goldman Sachs ( GS ), its stock tail-spinning from a growing fiasco linked to giant Malaysian investment fund 1MDB, sought to end a nine-day selling streak. The Dow Jones industrial average component gained more than 4 points to 172.81, but still lies nearly 37% below 52-week highs.
Apple ( AAPL ) is also trying to stem its waterfall decline. Shares in the iPhone and Apple Watch giant rallied more than 3 points to 167.06 in below-average volume.
Notice how the relative strength line, drawn in blue on all IBD charts and in MarketSmith , has fallen steeply for more than five weeks. This means Apple has sharply underperformed vs. the S&P 500.
After The Close Micron Technology ( MU ) reports fiscal first-quarter results after the close. The Street sees profit in the November-ended quarter jumping 21% to $2.96 a share. In the prior three quarters, the memory-chip expert has grown earnings per share 213%, 94% and 75% vs. year-earlier levels. So a 21% increase would mark continued growth deceleration.
Micron still trades well below its 200-day moving average. The stock also lies 46% beneath 52-week highs. So it is in no place yet to stage a potential breakout.
